This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

0 # lazygit

A simple terminal UI for git commands. ## Description Lazygit is a terminal UI for git commands that makes working with git easier and more intuitive. Instead of typing complex git commands, you can use a simple visual interface to perform common git operations. ## Features ### Stage individual lines Press space on the selected line to stage it, or press `v` to start selecting a range of lines. You can also press `a` to select the entirety of the current hunk. ### Interactive Rebase Press `i` to start an interactive rebase. Then squash (`s`), fixup (`f`), drop (`d`), edit (`e`), move up (`ctrl+k`) or move down (`ctrl+j`) any of TODO commits, before continuing the rebase by bringing up the rebase options menu with `m` and then selecting `continue`. ### Cherry-pick Press `shift+c` on a commit to copy it and press `shift+v` to paste (cherry-pick) it. ### Bisect Press `b` in the commits view to mark a commit as good/bad in order to begin a git bisect. ### Nuke the working tree For when you really want to just get rid of anything that shows up when you run `git status`, press `shift+d` to bring up the reset options menu and then select the 'nuke' option. ### Amend an old commit Pressing `shift+a` on any commit will amend that commit with the currently staged changes (running an interactive rebase in the background). ### Filter You can filter a view with `/`. For example, filter down the branches view and then hit `enter` to view its commits. ### Worktrees You can create worktrees to have multiple branches going at once without the need for stashing or creating WIP commits when switching between them. Press `w` in the branches view to create a worktree from the selected branch and switch to it. ### Undo Lazygit provides powerful undo capabilities. See the documentation for details. ### Commit graph Lazygit displays a visual commit graph showing the relationship between commits. ## Installation Lazygit is available through various package managers: ### Binary Releases Download pre-built binaries from the releases page. ### Homebrew (macOS and Linux) ```sh brew install lazygit ``` ### MacPorts (macOS) ```sh sudo port install lazygit ``` ### Scoop (Windows) ```sh scoop install lazygit ``` ### Chocolatey (Windows) ```sh choco install lazygit ``` ### Winget (Windows) ```sh winget install -e --id=JesseDuffield.lazygit ``` ### Arch Linux ```sh sudo pacman -S lazygit ``` ### Fedora / CentOS Stream ```sh sudo dnf install lazygit ``` ### Debian and Ubuntu ```sh sudo apt install lazygit ``` ### NixOS ```sh nix-env -iA nixpkgs.lazygit ``` ### FreeBSD ```sh pkg install lazygit ``` ### Conda ```sh conda install -c conda-forge lazygit ``` And many other package managers. Check your system's package manager for availability. ## Usage Call `lazygit` in your terminal inside a git repository: ```sh $ lazygit ``` You can also add an alias for convenience: ```sh echo "alias lg='lazygit'" >> ~/.zshrc ``` ### Changing Directory On Exit If you change repos in lazygit and want your shell to change directory into that repo on exiting lazygit, add this to your `~/.zshrc` (or other rc file): ```sh lg() { export LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE=~/.lazygit/newdir lazygit "$@" if [ -f $LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE ]; then cd "$(cat $LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE)" rm -f $LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE > /dev/null fi } ``` Then `source ~/.zshrc` and from now on when you call `lg` and exit you'll switch directories to whatever you were in inside lazygit. To override this behaviour you can exit using `shift+Q` rather than just `q`. ## Configuration ### Config File Location Default path for the config file: - Linux: `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` - MacOS: `~/Library/Application Support/lazygit/config.yml` - Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lazygit\config.yml` You can create repo-specific config files in `/.git/lazygit.yml`. Settings in these files override settings in the global config file. ### Keybindings Lazygit provides extensive keyboard shortcuts for all operations. See the keybindings documentation for a complete list. ### Custom Commands Lazygit has a flexible custom command system that allows you to extend its functionality with your own commands. ## Documentation For more detailed documentation, see the `docs/` directory, which includes: - Configuration guide (Config.md) - Custom command keybindings (Custom_Command_Keybindings.md) - Custom pagers (Custom_Pagers.md) - Undo/Redo functionality (Undoing.md) - And more ## FAQ ### What do the commit colors represent? #!/bin/bash
# usage: tui.sh <session> <dir> <cmd...>  -> starts session
# tui.sh key <session> <keys...> -> sends keys and captures
case "$1" in
  start)
    s=$2; d=$3; shift 3
    tmux kill-session -t $s 2>/dev/null
    tmux new-session -d -s $s -x ${W:-120} -y ${H:-40} -c $d "TERM=xterm-256color $*"
    sleep ${SL:-1.5}
    tmux capture-pane -t $s -p
    ;;
  key)
    s=$2; shift 2
    tmux send-keys -t $s "$@"
    sleep ${SL:-0.7}
    tmux capture-pane -t $s -p
    ;;
  cap)
    tmux capture-pane -t $2 -p ${3:-}
    ;;
  stop)
    tmux kill-session -t $2 2>/dev/null
    ;;
esac
EOF

for j in range(i0,i1+1):

EOF
done

package config

// UserConfig mirrors the structure of lazygit's configuration file. Field
// order matters because it determines the order in which keys are printed by
// `--config`.
type UserConfig struct {
	Gui                          GuiConfig         `yaml:"gui"`
	Git                          GitConfig         `yaml:"git"`
	Update                       UpdateConfig      `yaml:"update"`
	Refresher                    RefresherConfig   `yaml:"refresher"`
	ConfirmOnQuit                bool              `yaml:"confirmOnQuit"`
	QuitOnTopLevelReturn         bool              `yaml:"quitOnTopLevelReturn"`
	DisableStartupPopups         bool              `yaml:"disableStartupPopups"`
	CustomCommands               []CustomCommand   `yaml:"customCommands"`
	Services                     map[string]string `yaml:"services"`
	NotARepository               string            `yaml:"notARepository"`
	PromptToReturnFromSubprocess bool              `yaml:"promptToReturnFromSubprocess"`
	Keybinding                   KeybindingConfig  `yaml:"keybinding"`
	OS                           OSConfig          `yaml:"os,omitempty"`
}

type GuiConfig struct {
	AuthorColors                        map[string]string `yaml:"authorColors"`
	BranchColors                        map[string]string `yaml:"branchColors"`
	BranchColorPatterns                 map[string]string `yaml:"branchColorPatterns"`
	CustomIcons                         CustomIconsConfig `yaml:"customIcons"`
	ScrollHeight                        int               `yaml:"scrollHeight"`
	ScrollPastBottom                    bool              `yaml:"scrollPastBottom"`
	ScrollOffMargin                     int               `yaml:"scrollOffMargin"`
	ScrollOffBehavior                   string            `yaml:"scrollOffBehavior"`
	TabWidth                            int               `yaml:"tabWidth"`
	MouseEvents                         bool              `yaml:"mouseEvents"`
	SkipAmendWarning                    bool              `yaml:"skipAmendWarning"`
	SkipDiscardChangeWarning            bool              `yaml:"skipDiscardChangeWarning"`
	SkipStashWarning                    bool              `yaml:"skipStashWarning"`
	SkipNoStagedFilesWarning            bool              `yaml:"skipNoStagedFilesWarning"`
	SkipRewordInEditorWarning           bool              `yaml:"skipRewordInEditorWarning"`
	SkipSwitchWorktreeOnCheckoutWarning bool              `yaml:"skipSwitchWorktreeOnCheckoutWarning"`
	SidePanelWidth                      float64           `yaml:"sidePanelWidth"`
	ExpandFocusedSidePanel              bool              `yaml:"expandFocusedSidePanel"`
	ExpandedSidePanelWeight             int               `yaml:"expandedSidePanelWeight"`
	MainPanelSplitMode                  string            `yaml:"mainPanelSplitMode"`
	EnlargedSideViewLocation            string            `yaml:"enlargedSideViewLocation"`
	WrapLinesInStagingView              bool              `yaml:"wrapLinesInStagingView"`
	UseHunkModeInStagingView            bool              `yaml:"useHunkModeInStagingView"`
	Language                            string            `yaml:"language"`
	TimeFormat                          string            `yaml:"timeFormat"`
	ShortTimeFormat                     string            `yaml:"shortTimeFormat"`
	Theme                               ThemeConfig       `yaml:"theme"`
	CommitLength                        CommitLengthConfig `yaml:"commitLength"`
	ShowListFooter                      bool              `yaml:"showListFooter"`
	ShowFileTree                        bool              `yaml:"showFileTree"`
	ShowRootItemInFileTree              bool              `yaml:"showRootItemInFileTree"`
	ShowNumstatInFilesView              bool              `yaml:"showNumstatInFilesView"`
	ShowRandomTip                       bool              `yaml:"showRandomTip"`
	ShowCommandLog                      bool              `yaml:"showCommandLog"`
	ShowBottomLine                      bool              `yaml:"showBottomLine"`
	ShowPanelJumps                      bool              `yaml:"showPanelJumps"`
	ShowIcons                           bool              `yaml:"showIcons"`
	NerdFontsVersion                    string            `yaml:"nerdFontsVersion"`
	ShowFileIcons                       bool              `yaml:"showFileIcons"`
	CommitAuthorShortLength             int               `yaml:"commitAuthorShortLength"`
	CommitAuthorLongLength              int               `yaml:"commitAuthorLongLength"`
	CommitHashLength                    int               `yaml:"commitHashLength"`
	ShowBranchCommitHash                bool              `yaml:"showBranchCommitHash"`
	ShowDivergenceFromBaseBranch        string            `yaml:"showDivergenceFromBaseBranch"`
	CommandLogSize                      int               `yaml:"commandLogSize"`

	SwitchTabsWithPanelJumpKeys         bool              `yaml:"switchTabsWithPanelJumpKeys"`
}

type CustomIconsConfig struct {
	Filenames  map[string]IconProperties `yaml:"filenames"`
	Extensions map[string]IconProperties `yaml:"extensions"`
}

type IconProperties struct {
	Icon  string `yaml:"icon"`
	Color string `yaml:"color"`
}

type ThemeConfig struct {
	ActiveBorderColor               []string `yaml:"activeBorderColor"`
	InactiveBorderColor             []string `yaml:"inactiveBorderColor"`

	AutoRefresh                  bool              `yaml:"autoRefresh"`

	BranchLogCmd                 string            `yaml:"branchLogCmd"`
	AllBranchesLogCmds           []string          `yaml:"allBranchesLogCmds"`
	IgnoreWhitespaceInDiffView   bool              `yaml:"ignoreWhitespaceInDiffView"`
	DiffContextSize              int               `yaml:"diffContextSize"`
	RenameSimilarityThreshold    int               `yaml:"renameSimilarityThreshold"`
	OverrideGpg                  bool              `yaml:"overrideGpg"`
	DisableForcePushing          bool              `yaml:"disableForcePushing"`
	CommitPrefix                 []CommitPrefixConfig `yaml:"commitPrefix"`
	CommitPrefixes               map[string][]CommitPrefixConfig `yaml:"commitPrefixes"`
	BranchPrefix                 string            `yaml:"branchPrefix"`
	ParseEmoji                   bool              `yaml:"parseEmoji"`
	Log                          LogConfig         `yaml:"log"`
	LocalBranchSortOrder         string            `yaml:"localBranchSortOrder"`
	RemoteBranchSortOrder        string            `yaml:"remoteBranchSortOrder"`

package config

import (
	"bytes"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// Marshal renders the config as YAML using 4-space indentation.
func Marshal(c *UserConfig) ([]byte, error) {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	enc := yaml.NewEncoder(&buf)
	enc.SetIndent(4)
	if err := enc.Encode(c); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := enc.Close(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return buf.Bytes(), nil
}

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"lazygit-clone/internal/config"
)

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) > 1 && os.Args[1] == "--config" {
		b, err := config.Marshal(config.Default())
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		fmt.Print(string(b))
	}
}

import (

// Marshal renders the config as YAML using 4-space indentation.
func Marshal(c *UserConfig) ([]byte, error) {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	enc := yaml.NewEncoder(&buf)
	enc.SetIndent(4)
	if err := enc.Encode(c); err != nil {

	}
	if err := enc.Close(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return buf.Bytes(), nil
}

func murmur3_32(key []byte, seed uint32) uint64 {
	const c1, c2 = 0xcc9e2d51, 0x1b873593
	h := seed
	n := len(key)
	i := 0

		k = (k << 15) | (k >> 17)
		k *= c2
		h ^= k
		h = (h << 13) | (h >> 19)
		h = h*5 + 0xe6546b64
	}
	var k uint32
	switch n - i {
	case 3:
		k ^= uint32(key[i+2]) << 16
		fallthrough
	case 2:
		k ^= uint32(key[i+1]) << 8
		fallthrough
	case 1:
		k ^= uint32(key[i])
		k *= c1
		k = (k << 15) | (k >> 17)
		k *= c2
		h ^= k
	}
	h ^= uint32(n)
	h ^= h >> 16
	h *= 0x85ebca6b
	h ^= h >> 13
	h *= 0xc2b2ae35
	h ^= h >> 16
	return uint64(h)

		"java":    func(s []byte) uint64 { var h int32; for _, c := range s { h = 31*h + int32(c) }; return uint64(uint32(h)) },
		"sum":     func(s []byte) uint64 { var t uint64; for _, c := range s { t += uint64(c) }; return t },

	}

		"id":    func(s string) []byte { return []byte(s) },
		"lower": func(s string) []byte { return []byte(strings.ToLower(s)) },

	}

		"rand":    func(h uint64) float64 { return rand.New(rand.NewSource(int64(h))).Float64() },
		"rand2":   func(h uint64) float64 { r := rand.New(rand.NewSource(int64(h))); r.Float64(); return r.Float64() },
		"randInt": func(h uint64) float64 { return float64(rand.New(rand.NewSource(int64(h))).Intn(360)) / 360 },
		"mod360":  func(h uint64) float64 { return float64(h%360) / 360 },
		"mod1000": func(h uint64) float64 { return float64(h%1000) / 1000 },
		"mod100":  func(h uint64) float64 { return float64(h%100) / 100 },
		"mod256":  func(h uint64) float64 { return float64(h%256) / 256 },
		"mod255":  func(h uint64) float64 { return float64(h%256) / 255 },
		"mod65536": func(h uint64) float64 { return float64(h%65536) / 65536 },
		"div32":   func(h uint64) float64 { return float64(uint32(h)) / float64(math.MaxUint32) },
		"div64":   func(h uint64) float64 { return float64(h) / float64(math.MaxUint64) },

func murmur3_32(key []byte, seed uint32) uint64 {
	const c1, c2 = 0xcc9e2d51, 0x1b873593
	h := seed
	n := len(key)
	i := 0
	for ; i+4 <= n; i += 4 {
		k := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(key[i:])
		k *= c1
		k = (k << 15) | (k >> 17)
		k *= c2
		h ^= k
		h = (h << 13) | (h >> 19)
		h = h*5 + 0xe6546b64
	}
	var k uint32
	switch n - i {
	case 3:
		k ^= uint32(key[i+2]) << 16
		fallthrough
	case 2:
		k ^= uint32(key[i+1]) << 8
		fallthrough
	case 1:
		k ^= uint32(key[i])
		k *= c1
		k = (k << 15) | (k >> 17)
		k *= c2
		h ^= k
	}
	h ^= uint32(n)
	h ^= h >> 16
	h *= 0x85ebca6b
	h ^= h >> 13
	h *= 0xc2b2ae35
	h ^= h >> 16
	return uint64(h)
}

func Hsl(h, s, l float64) Color {
	if s == 0 {
		return Color{l, l, l}
	}

	var r, g, b float64
	var t1 float64
	var t2 float64
	var tr float64
	var tg float64
	var tb float64

	if l < 0.5 {
		t1 = l * (1.0 + s)
	} else {
		t1 = l + s - l*s
	}

	t2 = 2*l - t1
	h /= 360
	tr = h + 1.0/3.0
	tg = h
	tb = h - 1.0/3.0

	if tr < 0 {
		tr++
	}
	if tr > 1 {
		tr--
	}
	if tg < 0 {
		tg++
	}
	if tg > 1 {
		tg--
	}
	if tb < 0 {
		tb++
	}
	if tb > 1 {
		tb--
	}

// showKeybindingsMenu opens the "?" menu for the current context.
func (g *Gui) showKeybindingsMenu() {
	ctxKey := ""
	if g.currentWindow == "main" || g.currentWindow == "secondary" {
		ctxKey = "main"
	} else if ctx := g.currentContext(); ctx != nil {
		ctxKey = ctx.key
	}
	var items []*MenuItem
	add := func(section string, entries []kbEntry) {
		for _, e := range entries {
			if e.key == "<disabled>" || e.key == "" {
				continue
			}
			label := e.desc
			if e.opensMenu {
				label += "..."
			}
			action := e.action
			key := e.key
			if action == nil {
				action = func() { g.handleKey(key, keyEventFromName(key)) }
			}
			items = append(items, &MenuItem{Label: label, Key: e.key, Tooltip: e.tooltip, Section: section, OnPress: action})
		}
	}
	add("Local", g.localKeybindings(ctxKey))
	add("Global", g.globalKeybindings())
	if ctxKey != "main" && ctxKey != "status" {
		add("Navigation", g.navigationKeybindings())
	}
	g.showMenu("Keybindings", items)
}

// showKeybindingsMenu opens the "?" menu for the current context.
func (g *Gui) showKeybindingsMenu() {
	ctxKey := ""
	if g.currentWindow == "main" || g.currentWindow == "secondary" {
		ctxKey = "main"
	} else if ctx := g.currentContext(); ctx != nil {
		ctxKey = ctx.key
	}
	var items []*MenuItem
	add := func(section string, entries []kbEntry) {
		for _, e := range entries {
			if e.key == "<disabled>" || e.key == "" {
				continue
			}
			label := e.desc
			if e.opensMenu {
				label += "..."
			}
			action := e.action
			key := e.key
			if action == nil {
				action = func() { g.handleKey(key, keyEventFromName(key)) }
			}
			items = append(items, &MenuItem{Label: label, Key: e.key, Tooltip: e.tooltip, Section: section, OnPress: action})
		}
	}
	add("Local", g.localKeybindings(ctxKey))
	add("Global", g.globalKeybindings())
	if ctxKey != "main" && ctxKey != "status" {
		add("Navigation", g.navigationKeybindings())
	}
	g.showMenu("Keybindings", items)
}

#!/bin/bash
# reset a live original session to default state: close popups, exit search, go to first tabs, select first items, focus files
S=$1
tmux send-keys -t $S Escape; sleep 0.2; tmux send-keys -t $S Escape; sleep 0.2; tmux send-keys -t $S Escape; sleep 0.2
for w in 2 3 4; do
  tmux send-keys -t $S $w; sleep 0.25
  for i in 1 2 3; do
    # detect active tab index via title line colours
    idx=$(tmux capture-pane -t $S -p -e | python3 -c "
import sys,re
w='$w'
for line in sys.stdin.read().split('\n'):
    m=re.search(r'\['+w+r'\]\xe2\x94\x80(.*?)\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x94\x80', line.encode('utf-8','surrogateescape').decode('latin-1')) if False else None
    if ('['+w+']') in line:
        # strip to title segment
        seg=line.split('['+w+']')[1]
        # tabs separated by ' - '; active one wrapped in colour codes
        plain=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',seg)
        tabs=[t.strip('─ ') for t in plain.split(' - ')]
        # find which tab name is preceded by a colour start
        for i,t in enumerate(tabs):

        else:
            print(0)
        break
")
    if [ "$idx" = "0" ] || [ -z "$idx" ]; then break; fi
    tmux send-keys -t $S ']'; sleep 0.25
  done
  tmux send-keys -t $S '<'; sleep 0.2
done
tmux send-keys -t $S 5; sleep 0.2; tmux send-keys -t $S '<'; sleep 0.2
tmux send-keys -t $S 2; sleep 0.2; tmux send-keys -t $S '<'; sleep 0.3
